data.name: Devi
data.long_meaning: Devi is the Hindu goddess of fertility, motherhood, creation, and destruction. She is the embodiment of power, love, and compassion. In Hindu mythology, she is often depicted as the mother of all beings and the eternal source of the universe. Devi represents the divine feminine and is revered as the ultimate protector and nurturer.

data.cultural_impact: Devi is a revered and deeply significant figure in Hindu culture, often celebrated through art, literature, and festivals. This goddess is an icon of feminine power and is often represented as the wife or shakti of various gods, highlighting the integral role of the divine feminine in Hinduism. Devi is also a protector and is celebrated during various festivals such as Navratri and Durga Puja, where her forms are worshipped to seek her blessings for prosperity, health, and protection from evil.
data.spiritual_significance: Devi represents the ultimate divine mother figure, a loving and compassionate deity ever-ready to protect and nurture her devotees. She embodies the creative energy of the universe, bringing life and wealth to all beings. Through her various forms, she symbolizes the transformation of negative energies into positive ones, offering hope and redemption to those in need. Devi represents the eternal source of power, wisdom, and love, inspiring devotees with her grace and compassion.
